issues.issue: Is Harkat’s appeal from the interlocutory order denying state-funded counsel barred by IRPA s.72(2)(e) and s.82.3?
issues.applicant_position: Appeal should proceed without a certified question because the state-funding ruling is a separate act.
issues.respondent_position: Appeal is barred: no certified question, and interlocutory decisions cannot be appealed under IRPA.
issues.result_quote: I am of the view that the statutory bars on appeals from interlocutory decisions in paragraph 72(2)(e) and section 82.3 of IRPA apply to bar this appeal.

issues.issue: Does the separate, divisible judicial act exception (Tobiass), or a Charter s.7 argument, allow an appeal without a certified question?
issues.applicant_position: State-funded counsel ruling is a s.7 Charter act outside IRPA, so the Tobiass exception applies.
issues.result_quote: constitutional concerns do not, on their own, qualify as an exception to the certified question requirement

issues.issue: Do alleged ordinary errors of law permit an appeal without a certified question?
issues.result_quote: “ordinary errors” or “mere errors of law” will not permit an appeal to be brought in the absence of a certified question
